newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed on Thursday with a plunging domestic A share market pushing money back to the repo market, depressing early-maturing contracts, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract fell to 11.00 percent from 11.96 percent on Wednesday.
Turnover rose sharply to 16.69 million lots from 6.42 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Shanghai's A share index plunged 7.51 percent today on rumours that the government would take measures to cool the overheated A share market.
"If the A market continues to fall, the repo rates will also continue a downward trend in the next few days," a trader said.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on Thursday with the seven-year bond's poor debut depressing market sentiment, traders said.

The new bond opened at 99.90 yuan and closed at 98.60 yuan to become the first T-bond this year to trade below an issue price of 100 yuan due a shortage of liquidity at year-end. It was the day's most active bond on volume of 1.86 million lots.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market rose to 2.50 million lots from 658,579 lots.
